scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jeni Jol originated in the Skopje region of North Macedonia.

Its name is derived from the Turkish 'Yeni Yol,' meaning 'new road.' The dance is part of the čoček genre, which developed in the Balkans during the 19th century, influenced by the musical traditions of Ottoman military bands.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The name 'New Road' suggests a celebratory or transitional meaning.
It is a social dance that reinforces community bonds among Romani women in Macedonia.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by women in a curved line, holding hands and moving to the right.
It follows a 2/4 meter with a walking rhythm.
The core technique involves sensuous hip tilts that accompany a step pattern spanning six measures.
Watch for Hip Tilt.

The music is characterized by a slow tempo within the čoček genre.
